parts.label: (a)
hints: Hint 1: Think about the difference between doing a lot of work and doing that work quickly - which quantity measures how fast energy is transferred?
parts.proper_answer: Power is the rate of doing work, $P = W/t$, or the rate of energy transfer.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What Power Really Means**
Imagine two identical cars climbing the same hill, so they gain the same energy. One takes half the time. We say it is more powerful because it transfers energy faster. So power is all about speed of energy transfer, not just amount.

Step 2: **Examiner-Standard Definition**
Put that idea into words: power is the work done per unit time. In symbols: $$P = \frac{W}{t}$$ where $W$ is work done in $\text{J}$ and $t$ is time in $\text{s}$, so $P$ is in $\text{W}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Recall what kinetic energy depends on, and look carefully at what is said about the velocity of the car from A to B.
parts.proper_answer: Change in kinetic energy $= 0\text{ J}$ as velocity is constant.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link Speed to Kinetic Energy**
Kinetic energy depends only on mass and speed: $$E_k = \frac{1}{2}mv^2$$ Here $m = 1700\text{ kg}$ stays the same, and you are told the car moves at constant velocity from A to B.

Step 2: **No Change in Speed Means No Change in Energy**
If $v$ at A equals $v$ at B, then $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ at A equals $\frac{1}{2}mv^2$ at B. So: $$\Delta E_k = 0\text{ J}$$

parts.label: (b)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Focus on the force that opposes the motion and the distance pushed through it along the slope - work against it grows with both strength of force and length of journey.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Work Against a Steady Opposing Force**
When a constant force $F$ acts opposite to motion over distance $d$ along the line of motion, the energy you must supply is: $$W = Fd$$ Here $F = 440\text{ N}$ and $d = 25\text{ m}$ along the slope.

Step 2: **Substitute and Calculate**
$$W = 440 \times 25$$ $$W = 1.1 \times 10^{4}\text{ J}$$ This energy is transferred to heat by friction and air resistance.

parts.label: (c)(i)
hints: Hint 1: The extra $4.8 \times 10^{4}\text{ J}$ is stored as gravitational potential energy - think about which properties of the car and its lift determine the size of that store.
Hint 2: Use the relation between change in potential energy, mass, gravitational field strength and vertical rise, rearranged to make $h$ the subject before putting numbers in.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Connect Energy Gain to Vertical Lift**
Lifting a mass $m$ through vertical height $h$ increases gravitational potential energy by: $$\Delta E_p = mgh$$ It is vertical height that matters, not distance along the slope. You know $\Delta E_p = 4.8 \times 10^{4}\text{ J}$, $m = 1700\text{ kg}$ and $g = 9.81\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

Step 2: **Rearrange Then Substitute**
Make $h$ the subject first: $$h = \frac{\Delta E_p}{mg}$$ Then: $$h = \frac{4.8 \times 10^{4}}{1700 \times 9.81}$$ $$h = 2.9\text{ m}$$ to 2 s.f.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
hints: Hint 1: Sketch the right-angled triangle with the 25 m slope as the hypotenuse and the vertical rise $h$ as the side opposite angle $\theta$ - which trig ratio links opposite and hypotenuse?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **See the Slope as a Triangle**
The 25 m distance along the slope is the hypotenuse. The vertical rise $h \approx 2.9\text{ m}$ is opposite to angle $\theta$. So: $$\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{h}{25}$$

parts.label: (d)
hints: Hint 1: The engine must provide energy for two jobs at once - lifting the car to gain potential energy and pushing through the resistive force - think how to combine those two amounts to get total work.
Hint 2: Now link that total energy supplied to the given output power and the unknown time using the definition of power from part (a), rearranged for time.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Add Up the Energy the Engine Must Supply**
Since speed is constant, there is no extra kinetic energy. All engine work goes into potential energy plus work against resistance: $$W_{total} = \Delta E_p + W_{resistive}$$ $$W_{total} = 4.8 \times 10^{4} + 1.1 \times 10^{4} = 5.9 \times 10^{4}\text{ J}$$

Step 2: **Use Power to Find Time**
Power is rate of doing work: $$P = \frac{W}{t}$$ so $$t = \frac{W}{P}$$ With $P = 1.7 \times 10^{4}\text{ W}$: $$t = \frac{5.9 \times 10^{4}}{1.7 \times 10^{4}}$$ $$t = 3.5\text{ s}$$
